description: Canonical registry of callable Cloud Function names. Names use the domain.action convention per docs/api-guidelines.md; this file is the single source of truth for function names across iOS, Android, backend, and admin. Every callable verifies authentication context and, in production, enforces App Check — EXCEPT explicitly-documented pre-authentication endpoints (currently only diagnostics.submitReport) which are intentionally non-enforcing because they must work before the client can mint an App Check token; see each function's appCheck field and description. All callables return error codes from contracts/errors/errors.json. The status field tracks migration progress (planned vs implemented).

accessLevels.public: No authentication required. Reserved for telemetry that must work before sign-in (diagnostics.submitReport). App Check is non-enforcing on this path so a device that cannot yet attest (the exact failure it surfaces) can still report; a valid token is still verified best-effort. This is the ONLY callable that opts out of App Check enforcement (see submitReport.ts + appcheck-guard.test.ts).
accessLevels.signedIn: Any signed-in user, including suspended — reserved for cleanup paths that must work under suspension (e.g. push token unregistration).
accessLevels.member: Requires active member_monthly entitlement; suspension always overrides entitlement.
accessLevels.admin: Requires admin or owner role; does not require member subscription.

functions.name: auth.completeOnboarding
functions.description: Marks onboarding complete for the calling user; backend writes onboardingCompletedAt and consent timestamps. Deployed via grouped export as auth-completeOnboarding (functions/src/auth/completeOnboarding.ts).

functions.name: auth.recordLogin
functions.description: Stamps userLifecycle/{uid}.lastLoginAt = serverTimestamp() on each successful sign-in (trusted server write via the Admin SDK; userLifecycle/{uid} is a backend-only side collection — owner+admin read, all client writes denied by rules — so clients can never set it, and the account's activity is not exposed on the public users/{uid} profile). The Firestore field — not Firebase Auth's non-queryable lastSignInTime — is the queryable, admin-displayable last-activity source consumed by the scheduled account-cleanupInactive sweep. Active-actor gated (requireActiveActor): ANY authenticated, non-suspended, non-deleted account records lastLoginAt — non-members included — so an actively signing-in account is never wrongly treated as inactive; only accounts that have never signed in lack a lastLoginAt and are covered by the sweep's lastLoginAt ?? createdAt fallback. Idempotent (a repeat call refreshes the timestamp); the Android client calls it best-effort after auth completes. Deployed via grouped export as auth-recordLogin (functions/src/auth/recordLogin.ts).

functions.name: subscription.verify
functions.description: Receipt-verification entry point (authenticated). FAILS CLOSED with failed-precondition until config/subscriptionProviders.{apple|google}.enabled is set with real store credentials (end-of-MVP console setup; the legacy endpoint was itself a placeholder) - no code path grants entitlement from an unverified receipt. Raw purchase tokens are hashed (SHA-256) immediately and never stored, logged, or returned. Deployed via grouped export as subscription-verify (functions/src/subscription/verify.ts).

functions.name: live.startSession
functions.description: Starts (or RESTARTS with a fresh id/expiry) the caller's live location session with a chosen duration (1h|2h|4h), and clears any stale nearby-discovery doc. Sharing your OWN location is FREE: enforced by requireActiveActor (any authenticated, non-suspended, non-deleted caller) — NOT requireMemberActor, so this stays free even when member gating is re-locked; only VIEWING others is the paid surface. Gated by the liveLocation feature flag. Session state lives at RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/session - backend-only writes; owner-only read. Deployed via grouped export as live-startSession (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.updatePosition
functions.description: Writes the caller's latest position to RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/latest (lean marker node with denormalized displayName and session expiry) AND refreshes the queryable nearby-discovery doc liveSessions/{uid} (geoCell + last position + expiresAt TTL) that live.listNearby reads (the Firestore write is throttled to at most once per 60s, or immediately on a geoCell change, while the RTDB marker updates every sample). Sharing your own position is FREE: enforced by requireActiveActor (authenticated, non-suspended), NOT requireMemberActor. Requires an ACTIVE unexpired session; enforces the contract's 60-second staleness threshold. Markers are readable by any non-suspended signed-in viewer who is not blocked by/blocking the sharer — the RTDB read rule encodes only suspended + blocking, NOT an activeMember gate (member gating is disabled repo-wide, shared/memberGating.ts; a paid-viewing gate is added to that rule when re-locked). Deployed via grouped export as live-updatePosition (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.stopSession
functions.description: Stops the caller's session (status stopped, stopReason) and removes the latest marker immediately. Deployed via grouped export as live-stopSession (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.hideMeNow
functions.description: Immediately stops the caller's session (reason hide_me_now), removes the latest marker AND deletes the nearby-discovery doc liveSessions/{uid} — so 'hide me now' removes the sharer from live.listNearby discovery at once, not just from the per-uid marker read. signedIn access: works while SUSPENDED — removing your own position is a privacy action that must always be available. Deployed via grouped export as live-hideMeNow (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.extendSession
functions.description: Extends the caller's ACTIVE, not-yet-expired live location session ({} input — takes no client-controlled fields) by pushing expiresAt forward to a FRESH capped window (now + LIVE_SESSION_MAX_MS = 6h). This is the server side of the client's pre-expiry 'still sharing? continue?' prompt (shown 15 min before expiry). The new expiry is server-computed and server-clamped to the 6h hard cap, so a client can never obtain a longer window; only expiresAt changes (session id/displayName/mainCar carry forward, so no marker flicker). A session already past expiry (or stopped/expired) is failed-precondition — once expiry passes the extend path is closed and the client stop / 5-minute sweep stands. Free like startSession (sharing your own position needs no subscription); gated by the liveLocation flag. Deployed via grouped export as live-extendSession (functions/src/live/session.ts).

functions.name: live.listNearby
functions.description: Bounded read of ACTIVE, unexpired live sharers near a point ({ latitude, longitude, radiusMeters? }, radius clamped to 100..50000 m, default 15000), so a STANDALONE ('Single') live sharer is discoverable by users nearby even with no convoy/group roster carrying their uid. Open to ANY active signed-in user (requireActiveActor), mirroring incidents.listNearby: enumerates the grid cells covering the radius and reads only those from the queryable Firestore index liveSessions/{uid} (written/refreshed by live.updatePosition) via chunked `geoCell in [...]` queries (+ status=='active' and expiresAt>now), then filters to the exact server-computed Haversine radius. EXCLUSIONS: the caller's own session (self); anyone the caller has blocked or who has blocked the caller (block matrix resolved in both directions, reusing the convoy resolvePeerBlockPairs helper); expired docs; suspended users (enforced at write time — updatePosition requires a non-suspended actor, so a suspended user cannot refresh a discovery doc and ages out within the discovery TTL). Returns { sessions: [{ uid, latitude, longitude, displayName, updatedAt, expiresAt }] }, capped at 200; the client subscribes each returned uid's existing RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/latest observeLatest stream for live updates (which itself re-enforces blocking + suspension on the viewer). The high-frequency position stream stays in RTDB; only the geo index is in Firestore. Deployed via grouped export as live-listNearby (functions/src/live/listNearby.ts).

functions.name: drives.save
functions.description: Saves a completed drive: computes distanceMeters/durationSeconds/averageSpeed server-side from the submitted route points (implausible GPS jumps filtered), writes rides/{rideId}, and returns the canonical member-gated Cloud Storage paths (rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/) for the client route/preview upload. Idempotent per sourceSessionId. No top-speed is ever stored. Deployed via grouped export as drives-save (functions/src/drives/saveDrive.ts).

functions.name: drives.delete
functions.description: Deletes an owned drive: removes the rideRoutes/{uid}/{rideId}/ Cloud Storage files first, then the rides/{rideId} document. Available to any active owner — membership not required (legacy parity: free users can delete drives saved during a previous membership). Deployed via grouped export as drives-delete (functions/src/drives/deleteDrive.ts).

functions.name: blocking.block
functions.description: Blocks a target user for the caller. Directional and idempotent: re-blocking keeps the original createdAt; self-blocking is invalid-argument; blocking a missing/deleted user is not-found (never permission-denied, so deletion can't be probed). Writes userBlocks/{callerUid}/blocked/{targetUid} with the denormalized displayName. Returns the block summary plus shouldRefreshMarkers. Ports services/api/src/lib/blocking-service.ts. Deployed via grouped export as blocking-block (functions/src/blocking/manageBlocks.ts).

functions.name: blocking.unblock
functions.description: Removes the caller's block against a target user. Idempotent: unblocking a non-existent block returns { unblocked: false } rather than erroring; self is always { unblocked: false }. Deletes userBlocks/{callerUid}/blocked/{targetUid}. Ports services/api/src/lib/blocking-service.ts. Deployed via grouped export as blocking-unblock (functions/src/blocking/manageBlocks.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.submitClaim
functions.description: Submits a Kronjakt point claim with the full ported anti-fraud chain: feature flag, entitlement, idempotent replay (SHA-256-scoped key = claim doc ID), point availability, server-side geofence with accuracy buffer, <=1.4 m/s stopped-speed check, position freshness (<=60 s), repeat rules (once/daily/weekly), 10/day limit, rate/velocity/jump risk scoring (>=60 -> risk_review, no points). Eligibility failures return result codes with Swedish messages, not errors. Awards commit atomically with the claim record via the Kronpoäng ledger transaction. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-submitClaim (functions/src/crownHunt/submitClaim.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.createPoint
functions.description: Creates a draft Kronjakt point (title <=100, geofence 20-150 m, reward 1-1000 KP, repeat rule, optional availability window). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-createPoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.updatePoint
functions.description: Edits a draft or paused point (active/ended points are immutable); merged fields re-validated. Audited with changedFields. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-updatePoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.activatePoint
functions.description: Safety-gated activation: requires safeLocationConfirmed and an approval note (>=3 chars) recorded in the audit entry; stamps approvedAt/approvedByUserId. Ended points cannot be activated. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-activatePoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.pausePoint
functions.description: Pauses a point (ended points cannot be paused). Audited. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-pausePoint (functions/src/crownHunt/managePoints.ts).

functions.name: crownHunt.claimSpawn
functions.description: Collects an AUTO-SPAWNED Kronjakt crown (crownSpawns/{spawnId}) — the sibling of crownHunt.submitClaim, which collects a hand-placed admin point. Gated by BOTH the crownHunt flag and the crownHuntSpawn flag (contract default OFF), so a member can never collect from a system that is officially off. STATIONARY COLLECTION (safety-critical, and the main difference from submitClaim): the request must carry TWO position fixes, and the server checks that both are inside the crown's 75 m collect radius (accuracy-buffered, distances always server-computed by Haversine — a client-supplied distance is never read), that they are 4..300 s apart, that BOTH reported speeds are <= 2.0 m/s (7.2 km/h), AND that the speed the server DERIVES from the two coordinates and the elapsed time is also <= 2.0 m/s. The derived check is what makes the reported ones meaningful, since an absent speed is otherwise treated as safe. A failing claim returns the plain result code must_be_stationary with a Swedish message telling the member to stop safely and try again — deliberately NOT a risk flag, because the common case is an honest driver rolling through a car park. Nothing in this flow rewards speed: no time bonus, no arrival streak, no fastest-collector ranking. ONCE GLOBALLY, first-come: the first member to collect a crown takes it and it leaves the map for everyone (per-user claiming would make arriving first meaningless and would pay out a leaked coordinate once per member). Enforced INSIDE the ledger award transaction by reading the crown document and flipping it to status 'claimed' with expiresAt set to the claim instant, so concurrent taps serialize on the crown and exactly one wins; the pre-transaction status read is only a fast path. Per-user cap of 20 spawn claims per UTC day via a deterministic backend-only counter read and incremented in the same transaction (counted separately from the hand-placed points' 10/day). ANTI-ABUSE: the full shared chain — position freshness (<=60 s on the current fix), impossible-jump detection against the RTDB trusted position, GPS accuracy, attempts/minute and claim-velocity signals — scored by the SAME evaluateClaimRisk used by submitClaim, with the same 60-point review threshold; >=60 returns risk_review and awards nothing. Adds a mock-location signal (Android Location.isMock) worth exactly the review threshold, so a self-reported mock location alone sends the claim to review; it is one-way (absent and false are treated identically, since a spoofing client would simply not set it). Claims are idempotent — the document ID is a NAMESPACED SHA-256 scoping of (uid, client key), namespaced so a key reused across both claim flows cannot replay the other's result. Risk scores/reasons go to the backend-only crownSpawnClaimRisk collection and never reach a client. Awards go through the existing Kronpoäng ledger (source crown_hunt, deterministic idempotency key), never a direct balance write. Returns { result, pointsAwarded, newBalance, rarity, message }. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-claimSpawn (functions/src/crownHunt/claimSpawn.ts). SCHEDULED SIBLING - crownHunt-spawnCrowns (onSchedule, every 10 min, Europe/Stockholm; functions/src/crownHunt/spawnScheduled.ts): tops each ADMIN-APPROVED grid cell up toward an activity-derived target. Candidate set is crownSpawnCells where approved==true, ordered least-recently-served (round-robin, so a long allow-list degrades to a slower refresh rather than a starved tail), capped at 50 cells and 100 spawns per run. For each cell: A(cell) = sum over DISTINCT users seen in the last 7 days of exp(-dt/tau) with tau = 3 days (read from the backend-only crownCellActivity/{cellKey}/recentUsers aggregate, capped at 200 documents); N_target = ceil(1.5 * ln(1+A)) capped at 5, and 0 when A < 1 so a cell nobody frequents never spawns. Positions are rejection-sampled inside the ~1.1 km cell (24 attempts) against every live crown in the 3x3 neighbourhood, so no two live crowns are within 150 m — including across cell boundaries. Rarity is a weighted pick: common .70/10 KP/6 h, uncommon .22/25 KP/12 h, rare .07/100 KP/24 h, legendary .01/500 KP/48 h (TTL rises with value so a legendary is reachable while commons churn; every crown expires, so no coordinate becomes a farmable fixture). Crowns are marked source:'auto' and safeLocationConfirmed:false and carry approvedCellBy. Requires the crownHuntSpawn flag. SCHEDULED SIBLING - crownHunt-sweepSpawns (onSchedule, every 15 min, Europe/Stockholm; same file): deletes crowns whose expiresAt has passed — oldest-first, paged, capped at 1000 per run, mirroring incidents-cleanupExpired — including claimed crowns, whose expiry is set to the claim instant. Deliberately NOT flag-gated, so turning the feature off still lets already-placed crowns age off the map. Also recursiveDeletes crownCellActivity cells that have been quiet for the whole 7-day window, taking their recentUsers sub-collection with them.
functions.source: docs/migration/backend-domain-mapping.md (Kronjakt claims → callable functions + Firestore transactions)

functions.name: crownHunt.setSpawnCellApproval
functions.description: Admin allow-list control for Kronjakt AUTO-SPAWN: approves or revokes one ~1.1 km grid cell (crownSpawnCells/{cellKey}) for automatic crown placement. This is the HUMAN half of the auto-spawn safety model. A hand-placed point cannot go live until an admin ticks safeLocationConfirmed for that exact coordinate; auto-spawn picks coordinates by itself, so that per-point gate is impossible — and 'spawn where people already are' is NOT an equivalent substitute, because presence is not safety (a motorway is one of the most visited places in the country). The approval therefore moves up to the AREA: crownHunt-spawnCrowns reads ONLY approved cells, so an unapproved cell spawns nothing however much activity it accumulates. Input is { approved: true, safeAreaConfirmed: true (literal, so it cannot be satisfied by a default), approvalNote (>=3 chars) } or { approved: false, reason? }, plus EITHER cellKey OR { latitude, longitude } (exactly one, so a request can never silently target a default cell). Revoking is deliberately cheaper than approving — turning an area off must never be harder than turning it on — and it DELETES the live auto-spawned crowns in that cell immediately rather than waiting out their TTL, since revocation is the lever an admin reaches for after a near-miss and up to 48 h of standing legendary crowns would make it useless. Every call writes an adminAuditEvents record (crownHunt.approveSpawnCell / crownHunt.revokeSpawnCell) with the note, so every area ever opened has a named admin attached to it. crownSpawnCells is admin-read and client-write-denied in firestore.rules; it is not member-readable, because publishing which cells are approved-but-empty would tell a client where to wait for the next spawn. Returns { cellKey, approved, removedCrowns }. Deployed via grouped export as crownHunt-setSpawnCellApproval (functions/src/crownHunt/spawnCells.ts).

functions.name: events.create
functions.description: Creates an event. Writes the teaser-safe events/{eventId} document — which now also carries the PUBLIC map location (locationName + latitude/longitude) so every signed-in user sees event pins on the community map, a deliberate 2026-07 change — and the member-gated events/{eventId}/details/private document (long description + precise street address) atomically. Callable by an active member OR an admin/owner (admins never need a subscription; suspended/deleted callers are rejected). An admin's event is created as a draft plus an adminAuditEvents record, published later via events.publish. A member's event is stamped createdByRole 'member' + createdByUserId, has isOfficial forced false, must clear the same publish preconditions as events.publish (future start), is published immediately (post-moderation — admins take it down with events.cancel), is capped at 3 per member per rolling 24h (resource-exhausted beyond that), and writes no adminAuditEvents record: that log stays a record of admin actions only. Deployed via grouped export as events-create (functions/src/events/manageEvent.ts).

functions.name: events.update
functions.description: Partially updates a draft or published event across both event documents; cancelled/completed events are immutable. Writes an adminAuditEvents record with changedFields. Deployed via grouped export as events-update (functions/src/events/manageEvent.ts).

functions.name: events.publish
functions.description: Publishes a draft event after validating title, approximateArea, and a future start time. Deployed via grouped export as events-publish (functions/src/events/eventLifecycle.ts).

functions.name: events.cancel
functions.description: Cancels a draft or published event with a required reason; sets cancelledAt, never hard-deletes. Deployed via grouped export as events-cancel (functions/src/events/eventLifecycle.ts).

functions.name: events.complete
functions.description: Marks a published event completed ("ended"); going-RSVP attendees receive badge attendance credit (first_event / five_events, Phase 9f). Callable by an admin/owner OR by the member who created the event (createdByUserId); any other member is permission-denied. A member ending their own event writes no adminAuditEvents record — that log stays a record of admin actions. Events also reach completed unattended a few hours after they end, via the events-autoClose scheduled sweep (functions/src/events/scheduled.ts), which applies identical semantics including the attendance credit. Deployed via grouped export as events-complete (functions/src/events/eventLifecycle.ts). SCHEDULED SIBLING - events-remindUpcoming (onSchedule, every 15 min, Europe/Stockholm; functions/src/events/eventReminders.ts): reminds going-RSVP attendees that an event they are attending starts soon. Each run finds published events starting within the next 2h (EVENT_REMINDER_LEAD_MS) that have not yet been reminded — query status=='published' AND startsAt>now AND startsAt<=now+2h ordered by startsAt, served by the EXISTING status ASC/startsAt ASC composite index (no new index) — and writes ONE in-app notification under the event_reminder category (actionType open_event, relatedEntityId=eventId) to each events/{eventId}/rsvps/{uid} whose status=='going'. Push follows automatically via notifications-onNotificationCreated; the per-category opt-out and deleted/suspended eligibility are inherited from writeInAppNotification, not re-implemented (no blocking interaction — a reminder is about an event the recipient chose to attend). AT MOST ONE reminder per (event, attendee) EVER: primary guard is a per-event marker events/{eventId}.eventReminderSentAt CLAIMED in a transaction (re-deriving the due-decision against the fresh document) before any fan-out, so exactly one run fans an event out and every later tick skips at ~one read; secondary guard is a deterministic per-event notificationId (event-reminder-{eventId}) that collapses any re-fan-out into one inbox item. The marker is set once and never cleared, so editing an event's start time (earlier or later) never double-reminds. The runEventReminders(now) runner is exported for deterministic emulator tests.

functions.name: events.postChatMessage
functions.description: Posts a plain-text message (<=1000 chars) to a published event chat. Requires an active member with a going/maybe RSVP; enforces ~5 messages/30s per user. Writes events/{eventId}/messages with denormalized author display name. Deployed via grouped export as events-postChatMessage (functions/src/events/postChatMessage.ts).

functions.name: events.reportChatMessage
functions.description: Reports a chat message (reason enum + optional details <=500 chars). Deduplicates per message+reporter+reason; own messages cannot be reported; reporter identities are never client-readable. Writes events/{eventId}/messageReports. Deployed via grouped export as events-reportChatMessage (functions/src/events/reportChatMessage.ts).

functions.name: events.removeChatMessage
functions.description: Soft-removes (tombstones) a chat message (moderation): blanks the member-visible body, sets moderationState removed (a TERMINAL state), resolves open reports, and preserves the original text in an adminAuditEvents record. Never hard-deletes. Works from any non-removed state (visible / auto_hidden / allowed); re-removal is failed-precondition. Removed messages show a permanent moderator-removed placeholder with NO reveal control. Deployed via grouped export as events-removeChatMessage (functions/src/events/removeChatMessage.ts). TRIGGER SIBLING - events-onMessageReportCreate (onDocumentCreated on events/{eventId}/messageReports/{reportId}; functions/src/events/onMessageReportCreate.ts): chat AUTO-MODERATION. On every report write it recomputes the DISTINCT reporterUserId count for that message (report ids embed the reason, so one user filing several reasons is still one reporter) with a single-equality query (no new index) and, when the count reaches CHAT_AUTO_HIDE_REPORTER_THRESHOLD (default 3, tunable server-side in chat-core.ts), transactionally transitions a still-visible message to moderationState auto_hidden (body PRESERVED - auto-hide is reversible). It ONLY performs visible -> auto_hidden; allowed and removed are terminal and never re-hidden, and an already auto_hidden message is a no-op, so the trigger is idempotent and cannot race the report callable or a concurrent admin override. Clients render auto_hidden as a collapsed 'Show reported message' placeholder whose reveal is per-user ephemeral (never persisted, never un-hidden for others).

functions.name: events.allowChatMessage
functions.description: Admin override that CLEARS an auto-hide: transitions an auto_hidden (or still-visible) chat message to moderationState allowed - a TERMINAL state the events-onMessageReportCreate trigger never re-hides, so an allowed message can never be auto-hidden again however many further reports arrive (allow is STICKY). The body is untouched (the message becomes visible to everyone again), the message's open reports are dismissed (reviewedByUserId + reviewedAt stamped), and the action is written to adminAuditEvents. A removed message cannot be allowed (its body is gone) -> failed-precondition; re-allowing an already-allowed message is also failed-precondition. Input { eventId, messageId }. Deployed via grouped export as events-allowChatMessage (functions/src/events/allowChatMessage.ts).

functions.name: events.listChatReports
functions.description: Admin chat-report moderation queue. events/{eventId}/messageReports is backend-only (rules read/write:false), so this Admin-SDK collectionGroup scan is the only admin read path. Returns reports newest-first, ordered by the messageReports/createdAt DESC collectionGroup index over a bounded scan (single window, optional status refinement, pageSize<=100 — no page cursor yet), each including eventId + reporterUserId (surfaced to admins only). Deployed via grouped export as events-listChatReports (functions/src/events/moderateReports.ts).

functions.name: events.resolveChatReport
functions.description: Transitions one chat report to under_review/resolved/dismissed, stamping reviewedByUserId + reviewedAt and writing an adminAuditEvents record. not-found when the report is absent. Removing the offending message is the separate events.removeChatMessage callable (which also auto-resolves open reports). Deployed via grouped export as events-resolveChatReport (functions/src/events/moderateReports.ts).

functions.name: events.listAttendees
functions.description: Returns the roster of members who RSVPd to a PUBLISHED event, each with their answer (going/maybe/not_going). Requires an active member or admin; draft/cancelled/completed events return not-found. Joins each RSVP with the public users/{uid} projection (displayName, avatarPath) server-side and drops anyone in a block relationship with the caller (either direction). Read is capped at 1000 RSVP docs. Returns { attendees: [{ userId, displayName, avatarPath|null, status }] }. Deployed via grouped export as events-listAttendees (functions/src/events/listAttendees.ts).

functions.name: events.checkIn
functions.description: Records ONE position sample as proof of attendance at a published (or just-completed) event and, once the evidence is complete, marks eventAttendance/{eventId}__{uid} verified. Verification is GEOFENCE + DWELL, all measured server-side: each sample must be within 150 m of the event's own coordinates (haversine + a conservative GPS-accuracy buffer, reusing crownHunt/crown-hunt-geo.ts) and inside [startsAt - 30 min, endsAt + 30 min]; attendance needs at least two qualifying samples at least 10 minutes apart and at least 10 minutes of cumulative dwell (each gap credited at most 30 minutes). The client sends only { eventId, latitude, longitude, capturedAt, accuracyMeters?, platformIntegrityPassed? } - never a distance, a dwell or a point value - and capturedAt is freshness-checked against the server clock. Every sample runs through the same anti-fraud pipeline as a Kronjakt claim (crown-hunt-risk.ts evaluateClaimRisk: stale position, implausible jump vs the last trusted RTDB position, poor accuracy, attempts per minute); a score >= 60 records the sample as rejected and it contributes no dwell. Risk scores/reasons are backend-only and never returned. Rate-limited to 10 calls/minute per uid. No points are credited here - the points-onAttendanceVerified trigger awards event_attend_verified (50 KP, once per event) on the false->true edge, and event_host_success (75 KP) to the host once the event reaches 3 verified attendees. Intended client flow is two explicit taps ~10 min apart (one-shot GPS fixes, no background-location permission, no location trail), but the evaluation is written against a list of samples so periodic foreground posting works unchanged. Deployed via grouped export as events-checkIn (functions/src/events/checkIn.ts).

functions.name: garage.addVehicle
functions.description: Adds a vehicle to the caller's garage (max 5 per user, enforced transactionally). Schema: make/model/modelYear/powertrain/engineDescription/description/color plus registrationPlate — a DELIBERATELY PUBLIC, user-entered plate (Seb product decision) normalised server-side (trim/collapse-whitespace/uppercase, ≤12 chars, format-agnostic). VIN, insurance, and location remain unrepresentable because vehicles/{vehicleId} is authenticated-readable and those were never meant to be public. Deployed via grouped export as garage-addVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.updateVehicle
functions.description: Partially updates an owned vehicle, including setting/clearing imagePath (validated against the caller's own vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ prefix) and the intentionally-public registrationPlate (normalised server-side; null/empty clears it). Ownership failures return not-found to avoid existence probing. Deployed via grouped export as garage-updateVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.setMainVehicle
functions.description: Marks (or clears) one owned vehicle as the caller's main car. At most one main car per user is enforced transactionally — setting one clears any other. Ownership failures return not-found to avoid existence probing. Deployed via grouped export as garage-setMainVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: garage.deleteVehicle
functions.description: Deletes an owned vehicle: removes the vehicleImages/{uid}/{vehicleId}/ storage prefix first, then the document. Deployed via grouped export as garage-deleteVehicle (functions/src/garage/manageVehicle.ts).

functions.name: badges.adminSummary
functions.description: Returns aggregate badge award counts per catalog key (totalCount + last-30-day recentCount), ordered by the catalog. Aggregate-only — no leaderboard or individual user data. Badges live at users/{uid}/badges/{badgeKey}; client rules allow any authenticated user to read ONE member's wall (badges are public, so they can be shown off on a member profile) but no client can scan across members - that public read is per-member and NOT a global index, because Firestore authorises a collectionGroup query only from a rule written against a recursive-wildcard path (match /{path=**}/badges/{badgeKey}), while the public-read grant is nested under /users/{userId} and the only recursive-wildcard rule in firebase/firestore.rules is the deny-all catch-all; the emulator test 'no client can scan badges across members - collectionGroup is denied' pins it by requiring permission-denied for a viewer, an activeMember and an admin. So the summary is computed with the Admin SDK (which bypasses rules) over a collectionGroup scan. Ports the legacy SQL groupBy. Deployed via grouped export as badges-adminSummary (functions/src/badges/adminSummary.ts). The summary now covers 27 keys: the 5 original flat achievements plus 22 rungs across the 6 tiered ladders (Trogen has three rungs by product decision - no 365-day Platina - and Samlare has three because the garage caps at five vehicles). TRIGGER SIBLINGS - the tiered ladders (Kronjägare crowns / Vägfarare lifetime distance / Träffräv events attended / Trogen best consecutive-day app-open streak / Konvojledare convoys led / Samlare cars in garage) have NO callable at all, deliberately: a tier is derived exclusively from server-verified counters by six Firestore triggers in the badges export group (functions/src/badges/progressTriggers.ts), so a badge cannot be forged by any client request. Five source triggers bump one counter each on the backend-only badgeProgress/{uid} document - badges-onCrownClaimWritten (crownHuntClaims/{claimId} reaching result 'awarded'; a risk_review claim NEVER counts toward Kronjägare), badges-onRideCreated (rides/{rideId}.distanceMeters, computed server-side by drives.save), badges-onConvoyWritten (a convoy the member created that REACHED endedAt with at least one other accepted participant; crediting on start would make the ladder farmable with solo convoys, since convoys are born active), badges-onVehicleCreated (a server-side count() of the member's vehicles, stored as a running maximum so deleting a car never strips a tier; because it fires only on a CREATE, the same re-derivation also runs on the scheduled sweep below), badges-onUserLifecycleWritten (the Trogen streak, from the trusted-server-write userLifecycle/{uid}.lastLoginAt, counted in local Swedish calendar days) - and the SINGLE badges-onBadgeProgressWritten trigger then evaluates every ladder for that ONE member. That split keeps evaluation cheap (per-user, only when their counters changed; nothing ever scans all users on a write), complete (it also picks up completedEventsAttended written by the pre-existing events.complete attendance path, so Träffräv needed no change to the events domain) and loop-free (evaluation writes to users/{uid}/badges and pointsLedger, never back to badgeProgress). Awards are idempotent in three layers: the badge document ID equals the badge key and the write is a transactional create-if-absent; the per-tier Kronpoäng credit (25/75/200/500 for brons/silver/guld/platina, source 'badge') uses the deterministic ledger idempotency key badge_award_{key}, and is issued BEFORE the badge document so a crash between the two replays the credit rather than losing it; and qualification is a pure >= test over the current counters. Ladders are MONOTONIC - a higher tier never removes a lower one, and nothing in the domain revokes a badge. SCHEDULED SIBLING - badges-evaluateBacklog (onSchedule, every 6 hours, Europe/Stockholm; functions/src/badges/scheduled.ts): bounded self-healing sweep for the cases a trigger cannot cover (a permanently failed trigger invocation, counters that predate the ladders, a threshold/ladder added later so no counter changes, and SNAPSHOT counters that no increment can reconstruct). It walks badgeProgress in document-ID order (FieldPath.documentId()) from a stored cursor (badgeSweepState/backlog), at most 200 members per run, wrapping when exhausted - no composite index, and unlike a timestamp ordering it cannot silently skip documents missing the field. For each member it first re-derives vehiclesInGarage and then calls exactly the same evaluator the triggers do, so re-running it awards nothing twice. That re-derivation is what makes Samlare reachable at all for a garage that predates the ladders: badges-onVehicleCreated fires only on a vehicle CREATE, so a member already at the five-vehicle cap can never fire it again and would otherwise hold a full garage and no Samlare badge forever. It reaches every active member because auth.recordLogin stamps userLifecycle/{uid}.lastLoginAt on each app start, which creates that member's badgeProgress document. BACK-FILL SCOPE - Träffräv is retroactive (its counter predates the ladders) and Samlare is retroactive (re-derived here); Kronjägare, Vägfarare, Trogen and Konvojledare measure counters introduced by this phase, so they start from zero at deploy and accrue from activity onwards - historic crowns, rides and convoys are deliberately NOT replayed. runBadgeBacklogSweep(limit) is exported for deterministic emulator tests.

functions.description: Marks one in-app notification as read. functions.name: notifications.delete
functions.description: Deletes ONE of the caller's own in-app notifications ({ notificationId }) — the Android inbox's swipe-to-delete. The inbox is backend-write-only, so removal goes through this callable rather than a client delete, and the firestore.rules match stays read-only. Ownership is structural rather than checked: the document reference is built from the authenticated uid and the callable accepts no uid, so the only collection it can address is notifications/{caller}/items — another member's notification id names a document that does not exist there, and their item is untouched. A miss is a silent { deleted: false } rather than not-found (deliberately unlike markRead): the requested end state already holds, which makes a double-swipe, a retry after a dropped response, and a race with the retention sweep all no-ops instead of errors, and keeps the response from being an oracle for another member's inbox. The client removes the row optimistically and restores it when this callable fails, so a failed delete never silently drops a notification that still exists. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-delete (functions/src/notifications/manageNotifications.ts).

functions.name: notifications.deleteAll
functions.description: Empties the caller's in-app inbox and returns deletedCount — the Android inbox's "delete all", which the client puts behind a confirmation because it is irreversible. Takes no input at all and derives the collection from the authenticated uid, so there is no value a caller could supply that would reach another member's inbox. Batched at 500 and re-queried the way markAllRead is; the loop terminates because each committed batch removes the documents the next query would return. Idempotent (a replay reports 0), and a run cut short by the timeout is safe for the same reason — the committed deletes stand and a re-run finishes the rest. Deployed via grouped export as notifications-deleteAll (functions/src/notifications/manageNotifications.ts).

functions.name: diagnostics.submitReport

App Check is INTENTIONALLY NON-ENFORCING on this callable ONLY (unlike every other callable): the pre-auth telemetry path must still work on devices that cannot yet mint a Play Integrity token — the exact case it exists to surface. A valid token is still verified best-effort and recorded (appCheckPresent); a missing/invalid one no longer blocks the write. Abuse is bounded because writes land only in the admin-read-only private diagnosticsReports collection (90-day retention), all payloads are server-sanitized (tokens/credentials/coordinates/stack-trace keys stripped, bounded scalars only, SHA-256 dedup fingerprint), and the only public effect — the diagnostics-onSignInFailure auto-issue — is independently bounded by an allowlist + single Unknown bucket + per-fingerprint dedup. Deployed via grouped export as diagnostics-submitReport (functions/src/diagnostics/submitReport.ts).

functions.name: feedback.reportIssue
functions.description: Android "Report a problem" flow. AUTHENTICATED (non-suspended, non-deleted): unauthenticated callers are rejected with unauthenticated. Rate-limited to 5 reports/hour/user (resource-exhausted when exceeded). Persists the PRIVATE record of record to feedbackReports/{reportId} (admin-only read; carries the uid + client context + timestamp) FIRST so a report is never lost, then files a PUBLIC GitHub issue (labelled android-issue) on SebMcCayen/carcommunity via REST using the GITHUB_ISSUE_TOKEN secret. PUBLIC-REPO SAFETY: the issue body carries the user-entered description (public — the in-app UI warns users not to include personal info, and the backend does not scrub free text) plus only non-identifying context: appVersion/osVersion/deviceModel, the server report id and the submitted-at timestamp. The backend never attaches the caller's uid or any other server-side account identifier to the public issue. GitHub failures mark the doc githubIssueStatus:'failed' but still return success (never surfacing a raw GitHub error). Deployed via grouped export as feedback-reportIssue (functions/src/feedback/reportIssue.ts).

functions.name: errors.reportClientError
functions.description: Reports a genuine client-side RUNTIME error (e.g. the Messages inbox listener failing). AUTHENTICATED (non-suspended, non-deleted; no member entitlement required): unauthenticated callers are rejected with unauthenticated (pre-auth failures use diagnostics.submitReport). Rate-limited to 30 reports/hour/user (resource-exhausted when exceeded). Persists the PRIVATE record of record to clientErrorReports/{reportId} (admin-only read; carries the uid + bounded error context) FIRST, then writes an adminAuditEvents entry (action client.error, adminId=uid, targetId=fingerprint) so the error shows in the admin Audit Log. The errors-onClientErrorReport Firestore trigger then files ONE deduplicated PUBLIC GitHub issue per unique fingerprint (labelled auto-error + auto-generated) via the GITHUB_ISSUE_TOKEN secret, tallying occurrences in the server-only clientErrorIssueLinks/{fingerprint} collection so a recurring error never spams issues. PUBLIC-REPO SAFETY: the issue body carries only the feature key + app-generated message/code + non-identifying client context + fingerprint; the uid is NEVER attached to the public issue (it stays in the admin-only clientErrorReports doc + audit details). Deployed via grouped export as errors-reportClientError (functions/src/errors/reportClientError.ts).

Deployed via grouped export as account-deleteAccount (functions/src/account/deleteAccount.ts).

functions.name: subscription.grantEntitlement
functions.description: Audited manual entitlement grant/revoke (platform manual, reserved by the legacy enum) - the operational path until store receipt verification is wired. Applies the full chain with Phase 8 fail-safe privilege ordering: subscriptions/{uid} record, users/{uid}.activeMember, and the activeMember custom claim (revokes also revoke refresh tokens). Deployed via grouped export as subscription-grantEntitlement (functions/src/subscription/verify.ts). SCHEDULED SIBLING - subscription-expireLapsed (onSchedule, every 3 hours, Europe/Stockholm; functions/src/subscription/scheduled.ts): the EXIT from the paid tier. subscriptions/{uid}.expiresAt was written from day one by this callable (and by a store adapter when one is wired) but read by NOTHING, so an entitlement - including a manually granted one with an expiry date - never lapsed. Each run takes a single bounded query of subscriptions where status is one of the GRANTING statuses (derived from isSubscriptionActiveStatus, today active|grace_period - not hardcoded, so a new granting status cannot make the sweep silently blind) AND expiresAt <= now - SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRY_GRACE_HOURS, ordered by expiresAt ascending (longest-lapsed first) and limited to MAX_EXPIRIES_PER_RUN = 200; it NEVER loads the collection. Because a revocation makes the document stop matching, a backlog DRAINS across runs rather than recirculating - the same re-run-the-query-rather-than-cursor pattern as account-purgeDeleted, needing no cursor document - and every document in a page is processed, so one poison record consumes a slot instead of blocking the page behind it. GRACE WINDOW - 72h (SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRY_GRACE_HOURS in functions/src/subscription/expiry-core.ts), NOT zero: expiresAt is the renewal boundary, so every subscription sits past it for the window between the period ending and the renewal (or the store's status push) landing, and both stores retry a soft-declined card for days while the member is still paying. Revoking 72h late costs three days of access we were not owed; revoking an hour early takes away access a member PAID for. Erring long is strictly cheaper. REVOKES ALL THREE REPRESENTATIONS by calling the SAME applyEntitlement the grant path uses - subscriptions/{uid} record (status expired, entitlement none, platform/purchaseTokenHash/expiresAt carried through because that write is merge-less), users/{uid}.activeMember, and the activeMember custom claim - so it inherits the Phase 8 fail-safe ordering (claim cleared and refresh tokens revoked BEFORE the records, since a revocation DECREASES privilege). There is no fourth mirror of membership. IDEMPOTENT via three independent guards: the query matches only granting statuses so a re-run sees its own output and does nothing; decideSubscriptionExpiry re-derives the decision from the document and refuses to revoke on a result it cannot independently justify (the only thing standing between a mis-deployed index and a wrongful revocation); and the member notification uses a deterministic ID keyed on the LAPSE INSTANT, so a replay collapses onto one inbox item while a member who renews and later lapses again is correctly notified again. NEVER REVOKES ON ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE: a member holding entitlement with no subscriptions document, or one carrying no expiresAt, is deliberately untouched. That is what keeps a PERPETUAL MANUAL GRANT - the operational path today, since subscription.verify fails closed with no store adapter - from being revoked by a sweep that cannot tell 'granted forever' from 'record not written yet', and stops any future read failure or partial migration from becoming a mass lockout of paying members. Ending a perpetual grant stays an explicit subscription.grantEntitlement call with entitlement none. AUDIT TRAIL - each revocation is recorded at userLifecycle/{uid}.subscriptionExpiry { lapsedAt, expiredAt, previousStatus, platform, graceHours, source }, the existing backend-only per-user system-state document that already holds lastLoginAt and the inactivity-sweep fields; rules already deny all client writes and limit reads to owner+admin, and the account purge already deletes it. Deliberately NOT adminAuditEvents - those entries are keyed on an adminId and that log is a record of ADMIN actions (the same reasoning events.complete applies to a member ending their own event); a system-initiated revocation has no admin actor. No new collection is introduced. The stamp is written BEFORE the revocation on purpose: the two writes cannot be atomic (one touches Auth), and this is the recoverable order - a failed stamp revokes nothing and the document still matches so the step retries, while the reverse order would lose the audit record permanently because a successful revocation removes the document from the query. MEMBER NOTICE - one in-app notification under the pre-existing subscription_status category (actionType open_subscription), so no new category, contract enum, Android parser branch or settings entry is needed; push follows automatically via notifications-onNotificationCreated, and the per-category opt-out plus deleted/suspended eligibility are inherited from writeInAppNotification. NO EMAIL - email is deferred project-wide to inactive-account warnings only. Notification failure is logged and swallowed: a member must never keep entitlement because their inbox write failed. An ORPHANED record (account deleted, but subscriptions/{uid} is purged by neither the deletion doc-tree sweep nor the owned-document sweep) is closed record-only with a MERGING set - no claim, user document or lifecycle stamp to touch - so it stops recirculating instead of throwing auth/user-not-found in every future run. THE ORPHAN TEST ASKS AUTH (adminAuth.getUser), not Firestore: a missing users/{uid} document is NOT proof the account is gone, because account-purgeDeleted deletes the doc trees BEFORE the Auth user, so a live account still carrying the activeMember claim can sit in exactly that state - and closing it record-only would drop it out of this query, leaving the claim (which firestore.rules, storage.rules and database.rules all honour) standing forever. Only auth/user-not-found means orphan; every other Auth failure (quota, network, auth/internal-error, auth/invalid-uid from a malformed document ID) is a failure to ANSWER the question rather than a negative answer, so it is counted as failed and the record is left granting for the next run to retry. The test replaces the Firestore read the sweep previously did, so it remains one lookup per candidate inside the bounded page, and it runs BEFORE the lifecycle stamp so an orphan is closed without resurrecting the userLifecycle document the purge already erased. MEMBER GATING IS STILL OFF (shared/memberGating.ts MEMBER_GATING_ENABLED === false), so a revocation removes no capability yet; this builds the exit so it is correct and tested BEFORE the gate is flipped, which stays a separate atomic five-switch change. REQUIRES a composite index on subscriptions (status ASC, expiresAt ASC) - added to firebase/firestore.indexes.json, deploy on merge. runSubscriptionExpirySweep(now) is exported for deterministic emulator tests.
