functions.description: Issues a formal warning: immutable moderationActions record (type warning) + user.warn adminAuditEvents record committed atomically, and a best-effort essential account_warning in-app notification attempted via the notifications writer (non-blocking — a delivery failure never fails the callable; delivered even to suspended users). Not idempotent across retries: each call writes a fresh moderation action + notice. Deliberate deviation from legacy: no users/{uid} status change — the target model has no warned access state and a warning never restricts access. Owner accounts can only be moderated by owners. Deployed via grouped export as admin-warnUser (functions/src/admin/warnUser.ts).

functions.name: admin.restoreAccess
functions.description: Restores a suspended user: clears the suspended custom claim, mirrors users/{uid}.suspended, and writes immutable moderationActions and adminAuditEvents records. Deployed via grouped export as admin-restoreAccess (functions/src/admin/restoreAccess.ts).

functions.name: admin.setFeatureFlag
functions.description: Sets one boolean flag on the flat config/featureFlags document (merge-set; other flags untouched). The key must be in the canonical list in contracts/features/feature-flags.json — the namespace is closed, unknown keys are invalid-argument. The write commits atomically with an adminAuditEvents record. Clients read the document directly (authenticated, rules-gated) and fall back to contract defaults. Deployed via grouped export as admin-setFeatureFlag (functions/src/admin/setFeatureFlag.ts).

functions.name: admin.setAdminRole
functions.description: Grants or revokes the admin custom claim and mirrors it to users/{uid}.role. No client self-elevation: callers can never change their own role, and owner accounts are never modified. Writes an immutable adminAuditEvents record. Deployed via grouped export as admin-setAdminRole (functions/src/admin/setAdminRole.ts).

functions.name: admin.purgeNeverOnboarded
functions.description: One-off, dry-run-first cleanup of never-onboarded accounts left by the historical display-name leak (their Google real name sits in the world-readable users/{uid}.displayName). Input { dryRun: boolean, confirmToken?: string }. Selects users/{uid} docs where onboardingCompletedAt is null/absent, HARD-EXCLUDING any admin/owner role (Seb's operator account is never selected even if its onboarding flag were null) and any uid in an empty-by-default safelist. dryRun:true deletes nothing and returns non-sensitive identifiers only (uid, createdAt, whether a userPrivate doc exists) plus the count and the admin/owner-excluded count — never the leaked displayName or email. dryRun:false REFUSES unless confirmToken === 'PURGE', then reuses the existing account-deletion cascade (account/scheduled.ts purgeUserData — Auth user + all Firestore mirrors) per account (idempotent), writes ONE adminAuditEvents record (action purge_never_onboarded, count + purged uids only, no names), and returns the count plus any failures. Deployed via grouped export as admin-purgeNeverOnboarded (functions/src/admin/purgeNeverOnboarded.ts).

functions.name: friend.sendRequest
functions.description: Sends a friend request to a user resolved by nickname (displayName, NOT unique) or by a resolved toUid. Nickname resolution: 0 matches → not-found, 1 → proceed, >1 → failed-precondition with reason AMBIGUOUS_NICKNAME and a candidates:[{uid,displayName,avatarPath}] list in the error details, so the client re-calls with { toUid }. Rejects self (invalid-argument), already-friends and an existing pending outgoing request (already-exists), and either-way blocks (failed-precondition NOT_ADDABLE, neutral so the block direction is never revealed). If the target already has a PENDING request to the caller, the two are befriended immediately (returns status 'friends'). Writes friendRequests/{requestId} where requestId is a collision-resistant length-prefixed SHA-256 over the ordered (fromUid, toUid) pair. Deployed via grouped export as friend-sendRequest (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.respondRequest
functions.description: Accepts or declines a PENDING friend request addressed to the caller ({ requestId, action: 'accept'|'decline' }). Only the recipient (toUid) may respond; a non-recipient or missing request is not-found (never permission-denied, so requests can't be probed); an already-handled request is failed-precondition. Accept writes users/{uid}/friends/{friendUid} for BOTH sides (re-reading live profiles) and marks the request accepted; decline marks it declined. Deployed via grouped export as friend-respondRequest (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.cancelRequest
functions.description: Withdraws the caller's own still-PENDING outgoing friend request ({ toUid }) — the counterpart of friend.sendRequest. Addressed by RECIPIENT, never by requestId: the doc id is derived server-side as friendRequestId(caller, toUid), so a caller can structurally only address a request they SENT and cannot name (or probe the existence of) anyone else's. Deletes friendRequests/{requestId} so a withdrawn request reads as never sent (the recipient's pending list simply loses the row) and the pair can send again later; established friendship is the source of truth for 'already friends', so a delete can never disturb one. Returns { cancelled } — true only when a pending request was actually deleted. Every other outcome (no request, already accepted/declined, self) is the SAME silent { cancelled: false } no-op rather than an error, so a double-tap or a retry after a dropped response is idempotent and the response is never an oracle for activity on another member's account. Does NOT unwrite the best-effort in-app 'friend_request' notification from the original send (that would need a new composite index over another user's notifications; the actionable pending-request row is gone, and acting on the stale notice not-founds). Deployed via grouped export as friend-cancelRequest (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.remove
functions.description: Removes an established friend ({ friendUid }). Idempotent: deletes users/{caller}/friends/{friendUid} and the mirror users/{friendUid}/friends/{caller}; returns { removed } reflecting whether the caller's own side existed (self is always { removed: false }). Established friendship — not request status — is the source of truth, so a later friend.sendRequest can re-friend. Deployed via grouped export as friend-remove (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: friend.list
functions.description: Lists the caller's established friends plus incoming and outgoing PENDING requests ({} input). Returns { friends:[{uid,displayName,avatarPath,friendsSince}], incoming:[FriendRequestSummary], outgoing:[FriendRequestSummary] } where each FriendRequestSummary is { requestId, fromUid, toUid, direction, otherUser:{uid,displayName,avatarPath}, createdAt } with the OTHER party projected for the UI. Owner-only server reads; friends are also directly owner-readable at users/{uid}/friends. Each of the three queries is bounded (friends capped at 1000, incoming/outgoing pending each capped at 500) so a large friend graph can't cause an unbounded read; cursor pagination is a possible follow-up without changing the response shape. Deployed via grouped export as friend-list (functions/src/friends/manageFriends.ts).

functions.name: userSearch.members
functions.description: Live member typeahead backing the 'find a person' field ({ query, limit? } → { members:[{uid,displayName,avatarPath}] }). MATCHING: case-insensitive PREFIX over the denormalized users/{uid}.displayNameLower key (toSearchKey in functions/src/friends/friends-core.ts), queried as the half-open range [key, prefixUpperBound(key)) — typing 'gt' finds 'gt_86' and 'GT86_swe'; a MID-WORD or trailing substring such as '86' does NOT match. Firestore has no substring/contains/full-text operator and a precomputed n-gram token array is deliberately not built, so prefix is the whole capability. Single-field range + orderBy on the same field, so NO composite index is required. BOUNDS, all fixed server-side: the normalized query must be at least 2 CODE POINTS (shorter → invalid-argument with reason QUERY_TOO_SHORT, distinct from a malformed payload so a typeahead can render 'keep typing' silently); the raw scan is capped at 30 documents; at most 20 rows are returned and the optional limit is CLAMPED to that, never honoured beyond it; there is no cursor, so the endpoint cannot be paged into a member-directory export. A per-uid fixed-window rate limit (90/min, counter doc memberSearchRateLimits/{uid}_{epochMinute} read by id and bumped with FieldValue.increment; expireAt carries a Firestore TTL policy) is enforced after validation and before the scan, and returns resource-exhausted. The caller's own row and restricted (suspended/soft-deleted) accounts are excluded, as is any user with a block edge to the caller in EITHER direction — a blocked row is simply ABSENT, with no marker, count or reason code, so a search can never reveal that a block exists or who set it. The response projection is an allowlist of exactly uid/displayName/avatarPath, built field by field, so email, role, activeMember, suspended, deleted and any future field on users/{uid} are invisible by default. Declared access 'member' (requireMemberActor). NOTE the declared access is what is enforced WHEN THE GATE IS ON: functions/src/shared/memberGating.ts currently sets MEMBER_GATING_ENABLED = false repo-wide, so the entitlement half of every 'member' declaration in this registry is presently bypassed and any signed-in, non-suspended, non-deleted caller passes. Suspension and soft-deletion are NEVER bypassed. Re-locking is the documented five-switch procedure in memberGating.ts; this callable needs no change when it happens, and must NOT grow a bespoke entitlement check — activeMember defaults to false on provisioning, so a local check would deny every caller and make the search dead on arrival while the rest of the app stays open. Exists as a callable even though users/{uid} is authenticated-readable because security rules can bound none of the above. Deployed via grouped export as userSearch-members (functions/src/users/searchMembers.ts).

functions.name: dm.sendMessage
functions.description: Sends a 1:1 direct message to an ESTABLISHED friend ({ toUid, text, clientId? }, text 1..2000). Requires an established friendship (users/{uid}/friends/{friendUid}) — else failed-precondition NOT_FRIENDS; rejects self (invalid-argument) and either-way blocks (failed-precondition, neutral). Creates or updates the canonical conversations/{pairId} (pairId = the two UIDs sorted + joined by `__`), appends conversations/{pairId}/messages/{id} {senderUid,text,createdAt,clientId?}, bumps the recipient's per-member unread AND the userPrivate/{recipient}.dmUnreadTotal aggregate in one transaction. Returns { conversationId, messageId }. The optional clientId is a client idempotency key ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, e.g. a UUID) used verbatim as the message doc id so an optimistic-send retry is exactly-once (a resend of the same clientId returns the existing messageId without re-bumping unread or re-notifying) and the live listener can reconcile the delivered doc against the optimistic bubble; messageId equals clientId when supplied. FCM push deferred to end-of-MVP. Deployed via grouped export as dm-sendMessage (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.listConversations
functions.description: Lists the caller's DM conversations newest-first ({} input). Returns { conversations:[{ conversationId, otherUser:{uid,displayName,avatarPath}, lastMessage:{text,senderUid,createdAt}|null, unreadCount, lastReadAt }], totalUnread }. otherUser + lastMessage are denormalized on conversations/{pairId}; unreadCount/lastReadAt are the caller's own per-member values. totalUnread mirrors userPrivate/{uid}.dmUnreadTotal (the badge source). A conversation whose counterparty is in the caller's blockVisibility/{uid}.hiddenUids mirror is OMITTED entirely, in both directions - a blocked DM thread is hidden and inert for both parties (blocking-onBlockWrite additionally blanks the stored lastMessage preview and clears unread). ONE document read for the whole inbox. Deployed via grouped export as dm-listConversations (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.getMessages
functions.description: Paginated newest-first messages for a conversation ({ conversationId, before? } where before is an ISO-8601 createdAt cursor, exclusive). Only a member of the pair may read; a non-member or missing conversation is not-found (never permission-denied, so conversations can't be probed). Returns { conversationId, messages:[{id,senderUid,text,createdAt}], nextBefore, hasMore } (page size 30). A blocked pair (either direction) is ALSO not-found, resolved against the authoritative userBlocks edges rather than the eventually consistent mirror, so being blocked is indistinguishable from the thread not existing. The messages subcollection is independently denied by firebase/firestore.rules (possible there because every message in one conversation shares the same pair, so the condition is constant across the query). Deployed via grouped export as dm-getMessages (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.markRead
functions.description: Clears the caller's unread for a conversation ({ conversationId }). Sets conversations/{pairId}.unread[caller]=0 + lastReadAt[caller]=now and decrements userPrivate/{caller}.dmUnreadTotal by exactly the cleared amount (never underflows) in one transaction. Non-member/missing → not-found. A blocked pair (either direction) is not-found too: the thread is inert, and its unread was already cleared and unwound from the aggregate when the block landed, so a second decrement must not happen here. Returns { conversationId, cleared }. Deployed via grouped export as dm-markRead (functions/src/dm/manageDirectMessages.ts).

functions.name: dm.reportMessage
functions.description: Reports a message in a 1:1 DM conversation ({ conversationId, messageId, reason: harassment|hate_or_abuse|spam|unsafe_driving|privacy|other, details? <=500 chars }). Caller must be one of the conversation's two members; a missing conversation and a conversation the caller isn't in both return not-found (parity with dm.getMessages, so the endpoint can't probe whether two people talk). Reporting your own message is invalid-argument. Ids are constrained to a single Firestore document-id segment (no `/`, no `.`/`..`, no reserved `__*__`) so a hostile id is invalid-argument rather than a traversal into another document. BLOCKING does NOT gate reporting either way. SNAPSHOTS the reported message (text + author uid/displayName + createdAt) into the report because DM messages are readable only by the two participants — rules give admins no read path into conversations, so a report holding only ids would be unactionable; exactly one message is copied, never the thread. Deduplicates per conversation+message+reporter+reason (repeat silently refreshes details only; never resets a report a moderator already actioned, and the response never reveals a prior report existed). Rate-limited to 10 NEW reports/hour/reporter across all report types (resource-exhausted). Writes moderationReports/{reportId} (admin-read-only, client-write-denied). Returns { reported: true }. Deployed via grouped export as dm-reportMessage (functions/src/dm/reportMessage.ts).

functions.name: convoy.create
functions.description: Creates a convoy and invites a list of the owner's FRIENDS ({ inviteeUids:[uid] (1..50), title? (1..80) }). Each invitee is validated: must be an established friend (users/{owner}/friends/{uid}), not blocked either way, and a non-restricted existing account — non-friend/blocked/missing/self/duplicate invitees are silently SKIPPED (never an error that would reveal a block). Writes convoys/{convoyId} (status 'forming') with the owner seeded as members[owner]={role:'owner',inviteStatus:'accepted'} and each accepted invitee as {role:'member',inviteStatus:'invited'}; memberUids=[owner,...invitees] drives the list read + rules gate; memberProfiles denormalized. Writes a best-effort in-app notification per invitee (system_notice category). Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary, invited:[uid], skipped:[{uid,reason}] } where reason is self|not_friend|not_found|duplicate (a block edge either way is surfaced as the neutral not_found, so the inviter can't infer who blocked whom). failed-precondition if no invitee is valid, OR if the caller is already an ACTIVE participant of another convoy (ALREADY_IN_CONVOY — one convoy at a time): the caller may not create a new convoy while they own, or are an accepted member of, any non-ended convoy. That check runs as a query read INSIDE the create transaction (convoys where memberUids array-contains caller AND status in [forming,active]), so two simultaneous creates cannot both land — the second aborts, retries, sees the first and is rejected (needs the [memberUids CONTAINS, status] composite index). Deployed via grouped export as convoy-create (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.respond
functions.description: An invitee accepts or declines their convoy invite ({ convoyId, action:'accept'|'decline' }). Only an invitee (members[caller].role=='member') with a still-pending invite may respond; a non-member or missing convoy is not-found (never permission-denied, so convoys can't be probed); an already-answered invite or an ended convoy is failed-precondition. Accept sets members[caller].inviteStatus='accepted' + joinedAt=now (the green dot); decline sets 'declined'. ACCEPTING is gated by the one-convoy-at-a-time rule exactly like convoy.create: if the caller is already an active participant (owner or accepted member) of ANOTHER non-ended convoy, accept is failed-precondition (ALREADY_IN_CONVOY) — the check is a query read inside the same transaction as the membership write, so a concurrent accept into a second convoy cannot also succeed; DECLINE is always allowed. If the convoy is already 'active' when the caller accepts (a late joiner), their live-location session is auto-started (see convoy.start / item 2). Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary, inviteStatus }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-respond (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.start
functions.description: The owner transitions a convoy forming → active ({ convoyId }), setting startedAt. Owner-only: a non-owner (including a member) is not-found (can't probe); a convoy not in 'forming' is failed-precondition. ITEM 2 — starting the convoy AUTO-STARTS a live-location session for EVERY accepted member (owner + accepted invitees), not just the leader, so 'everyone in the convoy can see everyone' without anyone tapping 'share live'. This reuses the live-share PRODUCER (live.startSession's write side) — the session's visibility is the EXISTING live-share audience (non-suspended activeMember minus blocks), NOT a per-convoy scope (a convoy-only audience would require a marker read/rules change, owned by the live-visibility investigation); the session is stamped with convoyId for future scoping. best-effort (a live-share failure never fails start) and it does NOT touch a member's pre-existing MANUAL session (skipped-if-already-active, so teardown never kills a manual share). Late joiners auto-start via convoy.respond. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-start (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.end
functions.description: The LEADER ends a convoy FOR EVERYONE ({ convoyId }) → status 'ended', endedAt set, and a summary computed + stored on the doc (durationSeconds from startedAt→endedAt, participantUids/participantCount = accepted members, distanceMeters null — no shared-route aggregation in this foundation). The summary is readable by ALL members (they read the convoy doc). LEADER-ONLY (ownerUid): this is the one hierarchical action in the domain, because it reaches into other people's drive and stops it — any accepted member being able to close everyone else's convoy is both surprising and abusable. A member of the convoy who is NOT the leader gets permission-denied with an explanation (they can already see the convoy, so not-found would merely mislead — same reasoning as convoy.clearDestination) and has convoy.leave instead, so nobody is trapped; a total OUTSIDER still gets not-found so a convoy cannot be probed. Leadership is not permanent either: a leader who wants out without ending it uses convoy.leave, which transfers leadership. There is NO admin override on convoys today. An already-ended convoy is failed-precondition. ITEM 2 lifecycle — ending STOPS the convoy-auto live session for each accepted member, but ONLY the session the convoy itself auto-started (matched by the convoyAutoStarted flag + this convoyId); a member's own MANUAL live session keeps running. NOTIFIES every other accepted member under the 'convoy_update' category (never email), so a group surface does not simply vanish. The Konvojledare badge credits createdByUid on the transition INTO ended, which happens exactly once whether that transition came from here or from a convoy.leave that ended the convoy — so the two end paths cannot double-count. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-end (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.list
functions.description: Lists the caller's convoys ({} input): { convoys:[ConvoySummary], pendingInvites:[ConvoySummary] } newest-first (bounded at 200 via the [memberUids CONTAINS, createdAt DESC] index). pendingInvites is the subset the caller still has a pending invite for (non-ended + viewer.inviteStatus=='invited'). ConvoySummary = { convoyId, ownerUid, title, status, members:[{uid,role,inviteStatus,joinedAt,displayName,avatarPath}] (inviteStatus is the green dot), memberUids, viewer:{role,inviteStatus}|null, livePositionUids:[uid] (accepted members — the uids the map subscribes to at RTDB liveLocation/{uid}/latest for live positions), destination:{latitude,longitude,label,setByUid,setByDisplayName,setAt}|null (the shared destination — see convoy.setDestination; survives end), summary:{durationSeconds,participantUids,participantCount,distanceMeters}|null, createdAt, startedAt, endedAt }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-list (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.leave
functions.description: An ACCEPTED member removes THEMSELVES from a convoy ({ convoyId }) — the "leave, the convoy carries on" half of the TWO EXITS a member is offered (the other being convoy.end, which closes it for everyone and is leader-only). Fills the gap convoy.respond cannot: respond hard-requires members[caller].inviteStatus=='invited' and throws failed-precondition once you have accepted. The caller's entry is deleted from members + memberProfiles and their uid removed from memberUids (all three written whole in one transaction), so their convoy read (rules gate on memberUids), their convoy CHAT access and their livePositionUids slot all drop together — the chat HISTORY is left intact for the members still in it. THE LEADER MAY LEAVE: leadership TRANSFERS to the longest-joined remaining accepted member (tie-broken by uid, so a transaction retry picks the same person), rewriting ownerUid AND members[uid].role in the same update and appending to leadershipTransfers[{fromUid,toUid,at}] (capped at 25). Every leader-gated action reads one of those two fields, so the successor inherits exactly the privileges the leaver held; blocking the leader instead would force them to end everyone else's drive to get out, and a leaderless convoy would be an orphan nobody can end that keeps consuming live-location writes. createdByUid never moves, so the Konvojledare badge still credits whoever CREATED the convoy. FEWER THAN TWO WOULD REMAIN (MIN_REMAINING_MEMBERS_TO_STAY_ALIVE) → the convoy is ENDED in the same transaction (status 'ended', endedAt, and the same computed summary convoy.end writes — computed from the PRE-removal roster, so the leaver counts as a participant), because a convoy of one is not a convoy and hiding "Leave" from a member of a two-person convoy would leave them with no exit at all. CONCURRENCY: the remaining-count test and the removal are ONE transaction and the caller supplies no count and no mode, so two simultaneous leaves cannot both be told "enough will remain" — they contend on the same document and the loser retries against the post-first-leave roster and ends the convoy instead. A still-invited or declined member is failed-precondition (nothing to leave; respond is their path); an ended convoy is failed-precondition; a non-member / unknown convoy is not-found (never permission-denied, so a convoy can't be probed); leaving twice is not-found. Leaving frees the caller to create/accept another convoy. ITEM 2 lifecycle STOPS the live session the convoy auto-started for the leaver (matched by the convoyAutoStarted flag + this convoyId; a manual session or one from another convoy is untouched), and when the leave ENDED the convoy it stops every remaining member's auto session too — which, together with the roster removal that drops the leaver out of livePositionUids, is what removes them from the other members' maps at once. NOTIFIES the remaining members through the same in-app producer invites use, under the 'convoy_update' category (someone left / a new leader / the convoy ended); never email. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary (built from the post-transaction state; viewer is null — the caller is no longer a member), remainingMemberCount, outcome: 'left'|'left_and_ended', newLeaderUid: uid|null }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-leave (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.invite
functions.description: Adds invitees to an EXISTING convoy ({ convoyId, inviteeUids: [uid] (1..25) }) as members[uid]={role:'member',inviteStatus:'invited'} — convoy.create takes invitees only at creation, so without this a convoy can never grow. ANY ACCEPTED member may invite, not the owner alone: a convoy is a peer group and the owner is frequently the one driving, so owner-only would make the common case (adding the friend who just phoned) impossible; every candidate must still be an established FRIEND of the INVITER (users/{inviter}/friends/{uid}), which is what keeps 'any member' from meaning 'any stranger'. Blocking is honoured both ways against the inviter AND against every other ACCEPTED member, so nobody can be pulled into a convoy with someone who blocked them. Skip reasons are the same neutral set as convoy.create plus already_member (uid already in memberUids); a block edge is surfaced as the neutral not_found. Bounded: max 25 invitees per call and a hard cap of 25 TOTAL members (MAX_CONVOY_SIZE) — an over-cap batch is refused WHOLE (failed-precondition) rather than partially applied. Membership + cap are re-asserted inside the transaction and memberUids grows via arrayUnion, so concurrent invites/leaves cannot clobber each other. IDEMPOTENT: if every requested uid is already in the convoy — including when a CONCURRENT invite added them mid-call — the call SUCCEEDS with invited:[] and reason already_member, because the post-state asked for is the post-state that exists. Ended convoy / caller not accepted / no requested uid addable AND none already a member → failed-precondition; non-member or unknown convoy → not-found. Writes the same best-effort in-app 'convoy_invite' notification per added invitee as convoy.create (one shared path, so an invitee's opt-out works identically). Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary, invited:[uid], skipped:[{uid,reason}] }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-invite (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.setDestination
functions.description: Sets or REPLACES the convoy's SHARED DESTINATION ({ convoyId, latitude, longitude, label? }) — the one place every member can start navigation to. Any ACCEPTED member may set it (not owner-only: the owner is frequently driving and the person who knows where the meet is often isn't whoever pressed create); last write wins, with the whole destination object written atomically so a new coordinate is never observable paired with the previous label. Server-validated: latitude finite in [-90,90], longitude finite in [-180,180] (NaN/Infinity explicitly rejected — they survive JSON round-trips and would poison downstream distance math), label trimmed and max 120 chars (over-length is invalid-argument, never silent truncation; blank-after-trim stored as ABSENT, not ''). setByUid comes from the verified auth context and setAt from the server clock — never client-supplied, or a member could attribute a destination to someone else; setByDisplayName is denormalized from memberProfiles like members[].displayName. A 'forming' convoy MAY have a destination (agreeing where to go is what happens before rolling); 'ended' → failed-precondition; caller not accepted → failed-precondition; non-member / unknown convoy → not-found (never permission-denied). Members READ it as ConvoySummary.destination on the convoy read path they already use — no new listener, no second source of truth. ARRIVAL is deliberately NOT tracked and NEVER auto-ends the convoy. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-setDestination (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: convoy.clearDestination
functions.description: Clears the convoy's shared destination ({ convoyId }), deleting the `destination` field. Permitted to the member who SET it or the convoy OWNER — clearing is strictly more destructive than replacing (it can leave members mid-drive with nothing to navigate to and leaves no replacement to explain itself), so setter-or-owner lets the person who made the mess undo it and gives the owner a moderation path without letting any member wipe a plan the group is following. Any other accepted member → permission-denied (they already know the convoy exists, so not-found would mislead). Clearing when nothing is set is an idempotent NO-OP, not an error (two people tapping at once is normal). Ended convoy → failed-precondition: the destination SURVIVES convoy.end untouched as a record of where the group was headed, so there is nothing live to clear. Caller not accepted → failed-precondition; non-member / unknown convoy → not-found. Returns { convoy: ConvoySummary }. Deployed via grouped export as convoy-clearDestination (functions/src/convoy/manageConvoy.ts).

functions.name: communityChat.post
functions.description: Posts a message to the single APP-WIDE community chat ({ text, mentionedUids? }, text 1..2000, mentionedUids at most 10 uids). Member-gated (active member; else permission-denied); rejects empty/oversize text and more than 10 mentionedUids (invalid-argument). Appends communityChat/global/messages/{id} {senderUid, text, createdAt, senderDisplayName, senderAvatarPath, mentionedUids} — the sender's safe profile is denormalized onto the message so the channel renders with no per-message profile lookup. @MENTIONS are resolved CLIENT-SIDE (displayName is NOT unique, so the server never parses names out of the text and guesses): the client's @-picker sends uids and the server VALIDATES them — dedup, drop self-mentions, drop uids that aren't deliverable active members, drop pairs blocked either way (all drops, never a rejection: those are races and must not fail the post). The surviving set is stored as mentionedUids (always present, [] when none) for client highlighting AND is the ONLY community_chat notification fan-out: each surviving uid gets an in-app 'community_chat' notice (per-category opt-out honoured by writeInAppNotification) with relatedEntityId = the message id; a message with no mentions notifies NOBODY. A deterministic per-(sender, 15-min window) notification id caps a repeat-mentioner at one notice per window per recipient. Backend is the sole writer (firebase/firestore.rules grants any active-member read, denies client writes). Returns { messageId, mentionedUids } (the accepted mention set). FCM push deferred to end-of-MVP. Deployed via grouped export as communityChat-post (functions/src/chatchannels/communityChat.ts).

functions.name: communityChat.list
functions.description: Paginated newest-first community messages ({ before? } where before is an ISO-8601 createdAt cursor, exclusive). Any active member reads. Returns { messages:[{id,senderUid,text,senderDisplayName,senderAvatarPath,mentionedUids,createdAt}], nextBefore, hasMore, lastReadAt } (page size 30). mentionedUids is the server-validated @mention set for the message ([] when none, and for messages posted before mentions existed) — the client highlights those uids without resolving anything. lastReadAt is the caller's own userPrivate/{uid}.communityChatLastReadAt marker (the client derives the unread dot by comparing the newest message's createdAt to it — no fan-out unread aggregate). Blocking is filtered in BOTH directions off the caller's blockVisibility/{uid}.hiddenUids mirror (the union of 'the caller blocked them' and 'they blocked the caller', maintained by blocking-onBlockWrite): a message from a hidden uid is dropped. ONE document read per call, never one per message. The pagination cursor is taken from the RAW page before filtering, so a wholly-hidden page tail cannot stall paging. The channel's LIVE window is a direct Firestore listener and is filtered client-side against the same mirror - a Firestore rule cannot filter a list query per-document. Deployed via grouped export as communityChat-list (functions/src/chatchannels/communityChat.ts).

functions.name: communityChat.markRead
functions.description: Stamps the caller's community last-read marker ({} input) at userPrivate/{uid}.communityChatLastReadAt = now (owner-only readable, alongside dmUnreadTotal). The client's newest-message live listener uses it to show/clear the unread dot (O(1) per user, no fan-out). This same marker is the signal consumed by the scheduled community-chat DIGEST (see below). Returns { lastReadAt }. Deployed via grouped export as communityChat-markRead (functions/src/chatchannels/communityChat.ts). SCHEDULED SIBLING - communityChat-digest (onSchedule, 18:00 Europe/Stockholm, daily; functions/src/chatchannels/communityDigest.ts): the community channel has NO per-message notification producer (its audience is every active member, so per-message notify is O(members x messages) spam); besides @mentions, the DIGEST is how a member who was not mentioned still hears the channel was busy. Each run writes at most ONE in-app notification under the community_chat category to each member whose communityChatLastReadAt is behind the newest message by >= COMMUNITY_DIGEST_MIN_UNREAD (3) messages. Cost is O(behind-members) per DAY (a userPrivate last-read range query + one count() aggregation per behind member - the messages themselves are never fetched, and caught-up members are never read), NOT per message. Double-notify is prevented by a per-member digest marker userPrivate/{uid}.communityChatDigestedUpTo (advanced to the run's newest instant on notify) plus a per-UTC-day deterministic notificationId; the per-category opt-out and deleted/suspended eligibility are inherited from writeInAppNotification, not re-implemented. No new Firestore index is required (both queries use automatic single-field indexes).

functions.name: convoyChat.post
functions.description: Posts a message to a per-CONVOY chat ({ convoyId, text }, text 1..2000). Member-gated AND accepted-convoy-member-gated: the caller must be in convoys/{convoyId}.memberUids with members[caller].inviteStatus=='accepted' (owner seeded accepted). A missing convoy or a total outsider is not-found (never permission-denied, so a convoy can't be probed); a still-invited/declined member is failed-precondition. Appends convoyChats/{convoyId}/messages/{id} {senderUid, text, createdAt, senderDisplayName, senderAvatarPath, mentionedUids} (denormalized sender profile; mentionedUids is always [] — this callable accepts no @mentions, the field exists so both chat channels share one message shape). Backend is the sole writer (firebase/firestore.rules grants reads only to accepted convoy members via a get() of the convoy doc, denies client writes). The in-app notification fan-out skips members in the poster's blockVisibility/{uid}.hiddenUids mirror, matching what the channel now shows them. Returns { messageId }. Deployed via grouped export as convoyChat-post (functions/src/chatchannels/convoyChat.ts).

functions.name: convoyChat.list
functions.description: Paginated newest-first convoy chat messages ({ convoyId, before? } where before is an ISO-8601 createdAt cursor, exclusive). Only an accepted member of the convoy may read (same gate as convoyChat.post; missing convoy/outsider not-found, still-invited/declined failed-precondition). Returns { convoyId, messages:[{id,senderUid,text,senderDisplayName,senderAvatarPath,mentionedUids,createdAt}], nextBefore, hasMore } (page size 30). mentionedUids is always [] here — convoyChat.post accepts no @mentions (the chat already notifies every accepted member, so a mention notice would duplicate one they get anyway); the field is present only so both channels share one message shape. Blocking is filtered in BOTH directions off the caller's blockVisibility/{uid}.hiddenUids mirror (the union of 'the caller blocked them' and 'they blocked the caller', maintained by blocking-onBlockWrite): a message from a hidden uid is dropped. ONE document read per call, never one per message. The pagination cursor is taken from the RAW page before filtering, so a wholly-hidden page tail cannot stall paging. The channel's LIVE window is a direct Firestore listener and is filtered client-side against the same mirror - a Firestore rule cannot filter a list query per-document. Deployed via grouped export as convoyChat-list (functions/src/chatchannels/convoyChat.ts).

functions.name: convoyChat.markRead
functions.description: Stamps the caller's last-read marker for ONE convoy chat ({ convoyId }) at userPrivate/{uid}.convoyChatLastReadAt.{convoyId} = now (a map keyed by convoy id, owner-only readable, in the same document as communityChatLastReadAt). Same unread design as communityChat.markRead - a per-user LAST-READ MARKER, never a fan-out counter, which on a convoy would mean a write per accepted member on every post. The client counts unread messages itself by comparing this marker against the bounded newest-message live listener it already holds, which is what badges the map shell's convoy bar chat icon. The map is CAPPED at 50 entries (chat-core CONVOY_LAST_READ_MAX_ENTRIES): unlike community's single marker it gains a key per convoy the member has ever opened, so markRead evicts the oldest markers past the cap - safe because a convoy that old has had its messages TTL-deleted (30d) and a missing marker resolves to 'nothing unread' against an empty channel. The cap is enforced PER CALL (read-compute-write), not transactionally: two overlapping markRead calls for different convoys can leave the map one over the cap, and the next call prunes an over-cap map back down in one pass, so it self-heals and can never ratchet upwards. A transaction was rejected because this runs on the hot path and an aborted transaction is a silently failed markRead - a badge left lit on a chat the member has read. Deliberately NO accepted-convoy-member gate, the one convoyChat callable without one: the write lands in the caller's OWN private document, grants no access, returns only the id it was handed and so cannot probe a convoy's existence, while this runs on the hot path (on open and again per incoming message while the channel is open). Returns { convoyId } - the stamped value is NOT read back, because the client learns its marker from the owner-readable userPrivate listener that already drives the count. Deployed via grouped export as convoyChat-markRead (functions/src/chatchannels/convoyChat.ts).

functions.name: chatchannels.reportMessage
functions.description: Reports a message in either CHANNEL chat ({ channel: 'community'|'convoy', convoyId (required for and only for convoy), messageId, reason: harassment|hate_or_abuse|spam|unsafe_driving|privacy|other, details? <=500 chars }). One callable for both channels because only the eligibility check differs. Eligibility mirrors each channel's read rule: community = any active member; convoy = an ACCEPTED member of that convoy (same gate as convoyChat.post/list — missing convoy/outsider not-found, still-invited failed-precondition). Passing convoyId with channel 'community' (or omitting it for convoy) is invalid-argument, never silently ignored. Reporting your own message is invalid-argument. Ids are constrained to a single Firestore document-id segment (no `/`, no `.`/`..`, no reserved `__*__`) so a hostile id is invalid-argument rather than a traversal into another document. BLOCKING does NOT gate reporting either way. SNAPSHOTS the reported message (text + author uid/displayName + createdAt) because channel messages are TTL-deleted (community 120d / convoy 30d) and a report holding only ids would go blank. Deduplicates per channel+scope+message+reporter+reason (repeat silently refreshes details only; never resets a report a moderator already actioned). Rate-limited to 10 NEW reports/hour/reporter across all report types (resource-exhausted). Writes moderationReports/{reportId} (admin-read-only, client-write-denied). Returns { reported: true }. Deployed via grouped export as chatchannels-reportMessage (functions/src/chatchannels/reportMessage.ts).

functions.name: moderation.reportUser
functions.description: Reports a PERSON rather than a message ({ reportedUserId, reason: harassment|hate_or_abuse|spam|unsafe_driving|privacy|other, details? <=500 chars }) — the escalation for behaviour that doesn't reduce to one line of chat. AUTHENTICATED-active gate (requireActiveActor, matching blocking.block/unblock rather than the member-gated chat callables: reporting harassment must not require a live subscription; suspended/deleted still rejected). Self-report invalid-argument; a reportedUserId that is not a single Firestore document-id segment (no `/`, no `.`/`..`, no reserved `__*__`) is invalid-argument; missing or soft-deleted target not-found. BLOCKING does NOT gate reporting either way. Deduplicates per (reporter, reportedUser) WITHOUT the reason, so a single reporter cannot fill the queue by cycling the reason enum — a repeat updates reason+details and increments `occurrences` on the one document, which also makes the row count for a target equal the number of DISTINCT reporters. Captures ONLY the target's public profile projection (displayName+avatarPath, snapshotted so a rename doesn't orphan the row) plus the tally — never their message history, drives or garage. A per-target aggregate at moderationUserSummaries/{uid} ({reporterCount, totalSubmissions, lastReportedAt}) is maintained in the same transaction for O(1) 'how many prior reports' triage. Rate-limited to 10 NEW reports/hour/reporter across all report types (resource-exhausted). Writes moderationReports/{reportId} (admin-read-only, client-write-denied). Returns { reported: true }. Deployed via grouped export as moderation-reportUser (functions/src/moderation/reportUser.ts).

functions.name: incidents.report
functions.description: Creates a crowd-sourced road incident ({ type: accident|roadwork|hazard|police|road_closed, latitude, longitude, note? }, note <=200 chars). Member-gated. Writes incidents/{id} with a computed geoCell (coarse grid key used by listNearby instead of a full-collection scan), source:'user', reporterUid, a server createdAt, and a per-type expiresAt TTL (police 1h .. roadwork 12h). Clients cannot write the collection directly (firebase/firestore.rules denies all client writes), so a report cannot be forged, backdated, or spoofed as a Trafikverket import. Returns the IncidentView { id, type, latitude, longitude, source, reporterUid, note, createdAt, postedAt, expiresAt, confirmationCount }. postedAt is null for a member report (its createdAt already IS the post time); it carries the upstream original post time only for Trafikverket imports (incidents-syncTrafikverket), whose createdAt is instead the 30-min sync instant. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-report (functions/src/incidents/report.ts).

functions.name: incidents.listNearby
functions.description: Bounded read of ACTIVE, unexpired incidents near a point ({ latitude, longitude, radiusMeters? }, radius clamped to 100..50000 m, default 15000). Open to ANY active signed-in user, not only members — the Waze-style map layer is shared by all users and this is a read. Enumerates the grid cells covering the radius and reads only those via chunked `geoCell in [...]` queries (+ status=='active' and expiresAt>now), then filters to the exact server-computed Haversine radius (a client-supplied distance is never trusted) and caps at 200. Per-user rate limited to 60 calls per fixed 60 s window (generous headroom over the ~10–30 calls/min a legitimate polling+panning client makes) to cap the FREQUENCY cost a client hot-loop or a valid-token abuser could run up — the per-call cost is already bounded (App Check, requireActiveActor, MAX_RESULTS=200, 50 km radius clamp). The limit is a cheap fixed-window counter (backend-only incidentListRateLimits/{uid}_{epochMinute} doc, read by id and bumped with FieldValue.increment, TTL-reaped via expireAt, no index) checked BEFORE the geoCell reads; on exceed it throws resource-exhausted (the client keeps its previous markers, so a throttled tick just skips a refresh). Returns { incidents: IncidentView[] }, each carrying postedAt — the upstream original post time for a Trafikverket import (its createdAt is the sync instant), null for a member report (whose createdAt already is the post time) or an import upstream sent no usable time for, in which case the client hides the age line rather than showing the sync time. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-listNearby (functions/src/incidents/listNearby.ts).

functions.name: incidents.remove
functions.description: Clears an incident the caller no longer stands behind ({ incidentId }). A signed-in caller may remove their OWN report; an admin may remove any (moderation). Idempotent: removing a missing incident is a no-op success ({ removed: false }). Imported (source!='user') incidents are failed-precondition for EVERYONE including admins — the Trafikverket sync would just re-upsert them. Deletes the document and its confirmations sub-collection (recursiveDelete) so the marker disappears for everyone on the next nearby fetch. Returns { removed }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-remove (functions/src/incidents/remove.ts).

functions.name: incidents.confirm
functions.description: Confirms someone else's incident is still there ({ incidentId }) — the 'is this still there?' action on a marker. Declared access 'member' (requireMemberActor), matching incidents.report rather than the read-only listNearby: it is a write that keeps a marker alive for every user. NOTE the declared access is what is enforced WHEN THE GATE IS ON: functions/src/shared/memberGating.ts currently sets MEMBER_GATING_ENABLED = false repo-wide, so the entitlement half of every 'member' declaration in this registry is presently bypassed and any signed-in, non-suspended, non-deleted caller passes. Suspension and soft-deletion are NEVER bypassed. Re-locking is the documented five-switch procedure in memberGating.ts; this callable needs no change when it happens. ONE confirmation per user per incident, enforced by the document id of incidents/{id}/confirmations/{uid} claimed with tx.create in the same transaction that increments incidents/{id}.confirmationCount and extends expiresAt — concurrent double-taps cannot double-count. A repeat is idempotent success with alreadyConfirmed:true (no second write, no further extension), not an error. The reporter cannot confirm their own report (permission-denied). Confirming resets expiresAt to a fresh per-type TTL from now, never backwards and never past the hard cap createdAt + 3x the type's TTL, so a confirmed incident persists but can never become immortal. A missing incident is not-found; an inactive/expired one is failed-precondition; an imported (source!='user') one is failed-precondition because runTrafikverketSync full-overwrites each tv_ doc every 30 minutes and upstream is the authority on whether it is still live. No notification is sent to the reporter (ambient corroboration, not a social interaction). A member who had voted the incident GONE (incidents.reportCleared) may SWITCH back by confirming: their clearVotes/{uid} ledger doc is deleted and clearedCount decremented in the SAME transaction that claims the confirmation, so a switcher is never counted on both sides. Every confirmation also RE-DERIVES the incident's reportedCleared flag from the resulting counts (evaluateClearVote), so a confirmation that brings confirms level with the clears un-fades the marker rather than leaving a stale true behind; the counts are written as absolute values rather than FieldValue.increment precisely so the flag can never disagree with the numbers written beside it. Returns { incidentId, confirmationCount, clearedCount, reportedCleared, expiresAt, alreadyConfirmed, switchedFromClearVote }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-confirm (functions/src/incidents/confirm.ts).

functions.name: incidents.reportCleared
functions.description: Votes that a crowd-sourced incident is NO LONGER THERE ({ incidentId, latitude, longitude, capturedAt, accuracyMeters?, mockLocationReported? }) — the 'Nej, den är borta' half of the 'Är den kvar?' question on the incident tap popup. Member-gated (requireMemberActor), matching incidents.report/confirm: it is a WRITE that changes what every user on the map sees. TRANSPARENT DECAY, NEVER INSTANT DELETION. One tap deleting a marker for everyone would let a single mistaken or malicious member erase a real accident or road closure; wrongly REMOVING a live hazard is far worse than briefly showing a stale one. So a clear vote WEAKENS the incident visibly: it increments incidents/{id}.clearedCount, and while clears LEAD but are below the removal threshold the incident stays on the map with reportedCleared:true, which clients render as a faded marker plus 'Rapporterad som borta av N'. BOTH counts (confirmationCount and clearedCount) travel to clients on every IncidentView, never netted into one number, so an arriving member weighs the two signals itself. NET SCORE + THRESHOLD: the effective signal is clearedCount - confirmationCount. reportedCleared is set when that net is > 0; at CLEAR_VOTES_TO_REMOVE = 2 NET clear votes the incident is REMOVED for everyone. Removal is done by setting expiresAt to now, NOT by deleting: the security read rule and listNearby both gate on expiresAt > now so the marker vanishes immediately, the existing incidents-cleanupExpired sweep reclaims the document and its sub-collections 15 minutes later (recursiveDelete), and the vote ledger survives long enough to explain why it went. Worked cases (unit-pinned): 1 clear + 1 confirm = net 0 = NOT faded; 1 clear + 0 confirms = faded; 2 clears net = removed. THE ORIGINAL REPORTER (and any admin) clearing it removes it IMMEDIATELY with no threshold — they have the best information about their own report, the same authority incidents.remove already grants, expressed as a vote so the ledger records it. ONE VOTE PER USER PER INCIDENT, enforced by the document id of incidents/{id}/clearVotes/{uid} claimed with tx.create inside the same transaction that writes the counters, so concurrent double-taps cannot double-count. A repeat is idempotent success with alreadyVoted:true, not an error. VOTE SWITCHING IS ALLOWED in both directions: a member who already confirmed may switch to a clear vote (their confirmations/{uid} doc is deleted and confirmationCount decremented in the same transaction, switchedFromConfirmation:true), and incidents.confirm handles the mirror. Allowed deliberately — refusing it would leave a stale confirmation propping up a marker the voter now knows is wrong, and a switch is still one vote, still needs physical presence, still passes risk and rate limits. PROXIMITY (safety-critical): you must be NEAR the incident. Distance is always server-computed by the shared crownHunt haversineDistanceMeters from the STORED incident position and the reported fix — a client-supplied distance is never read — and checked with the shared isWithinGeofence against INCIDENT_CLEAR_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_METERS = 300 m (wider than the events 150 m fence because an incident is passed at speed). The client-supplied accuracyMeters that BUFFERS that fence is bounded twice inside isWithinGeofence (clamped to MAX_GEOFENCE_ACCURACY_METERS = 100, effective radius capped at 2x, PR #573) AND independently at this callable's own zod input boundary (MAX_REPORTED_ACCURACY_METERS = 10000, the same constant crownHunt uses; zod 4 already rejects NaN/Infinity), so the effective fence is provably within [300, 350] m and the callable is safe even if the shared helper is ever relaxed. The fix's own capturedAt is checked with isPositionFresh, and the whole sample is scored by the SAME evaluateClaimRisk and the same RISK_REVIEW_THRESHOLD (60) as a Kronjakt claim — freshness, poor accuracy, attempts/minute, self-reported mock location — with a high-risk sample counting NO vote. Risk scores/reasons go to the backend-only incidentClearVoteRisk collection and NEVER reach a client. Per-user fixed-window rate limit of 6 calls/60 s via the backend-only incidentClearRateLimits/{uid}_{epochMinute} counter (read by id, FieldValue.increment, expireAt TTL, no index), in its OWN collection so map refreshes cannot starve voting. IMPORTED (source != 'user') INCIDENTS ARE REJECTED for everyone: runTrafikverketSync full-overwrites each tv_ doc with a merge-less batch.set every 30 minutes, so a member vote would simply be wiped, and upstream is the authority on whether the situation is still live. Rejected with failed-precondition and details.reason = 'imported_incident' so the client can explain why ('Uppgiften kommer från Trafikverket') instead of showing a generic failure. REJECTIONS carry a machine-readable details.reason from a small closed set: imported_incident, incident_inactive, out_of_range (failed-precondition), position_too_old (failed-precondition), vote_not_counted (permission-denied, and deliberately says nothing about WHICH risk signal tripped). A missing incident is not-found. Returns { incidentId, clearedCount, confirmationCount, reportedCleared, removed, alreadyVoted, switchedFromConfirmation }. Deployed via grouped export as incidents-reportCleared (functions/src/incidents/reportCleared.ts).

functions.name: finance.estimate
functions.description: Admin-only on-demand cost estimate in SEK ({} input — takes no client-controlled fields). Computes an IN-APP COST MODEL (estimated, NOT the real Google Cloud bill): a sourced+dated price table (functions/src/finance/pricing.ts), labelled usage assumptions (assumptions.ts), and the function inventory (inventory.ts). Reads the latest metrics/{YYYY-MM-DD} snapshot's totalUsers for the LIVE member count so the variable half tracks community growth (falls back to a labelled default with source:'fallback' when no snapshot exists yet). Splits cost into two honest halves: COMMITTED (scheduled jobs — cadence x per-run work, independent of members; Trafikverket's ~2,775 writes/run x 48 runs/day dominates) and VARIABLE (per-member Firestore/Functions/RTDB/Storage usage). Applies each service's free tier explicitly (gross -> free -> billable -> SEK). Returns a Google Cloud subtotal, a SEPARATE Mapbox vendor estimate (never blended in), and a SEPARATE fixed-subscriptions section (e.g. Claude — placeholder until Seb sets his real plan cost), plus a grand total and any uncosted functions. On-demand rather than scheduled on purpose: no history is needed, so it avoids adding a scheduled Firestore write (a cost of its own). Every figure is a MODEL ESTIMATE; the admin page carries that banner and links to the Google Cloud billing console. Deployed via grouped export as finance-estimate (functions/src/finance/estimate.ts).
